lines.text: You are implementing Samanvay, a clearly labelled student prototype for institution-related complaint coordination across AICTE bureaus. Its value proposition is: “See connected complaints, responsible officers, and next actions across bureaus in one institution view.” The supplied brief names PS 26264. Verify that identifier, the exact official statement, competition year, and submission requirements when an authoritative source is available. Do not invent confirmation or silently substitute a different statement.

Treat the supplied requirements as the implementation contract. Use fictional institutions, synthetic complainants, and synthetic identifiers. Do not access restricted AICTE systems, imply deployment or endorsement, incur charges, or send external messages without authorization. Missing official access should produce labelled adapters and documented assumptions, not fake integrations.

Inspect the repository and environment. Prefer existing conventions; otherwise use a conventional modular application, such as React/TypeScript, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL with migrations. Choose compatible versions and record exact setup commands. Use a real database, persistent attachments, backend validation, and background processing. Keep the core demo usable without paid API keys. Do not claim a framework, model, or database is available until inspected.
Preserve these invariants:
1. Confirmed same institution plus active cases in different bureaus generates a coordination item regardless of complaint similarity.
2. Duplicate submission, related complaint, independent complaint, and UNKNOWN are separate relationship outcomes. Same institution never means automatic duplication.
3. Authorized humans confirm relationships and coordination decisions. AI must not merge, discard, close, transfer, or adjudicate cases.
4. Original records and evidence remain intact. Preserve case identity during transfer; retain the accountable source owner until the target accepts.
5. Lifecycle state, owner, transfer state, overdue condition, and escalation level are distinct.
6. Authorization applies to APIs, attachment bytes, search, matching evidence, notifications, dashboard counts, and exports. Hidden buttons are insufficient.
7. Case changes and audit records commit together. Use version checks and transactions to prevent silent conflicting updates.
8. Display only observed results. Label targets, illustrative rules, synthetic data, unavailable services, and proposed policies accurately.

Maintain PROJECT_STATE.md with the current stage, completed features, known failures, actual commands and results, decisions, and next actions. Maintain REQUIREMENTS.md with original requirement, implementation location, acceptance test, and evidence. Record policy decisions in DECISIONS.md. Do not repeatedly rewrite working architecture or restart the project because context changed.

For every stage, implement and run the relevant checks. Report what changed, what worked, what failed, and the next acceptance gate. A written test is not a passed test; a screenshot is not proof of persistence. Fix material failures before declaring completion. Continue independent work when a missing answer affects only part of the project.
STAGE 0 — ESTABLISH VERIFIED SCOPE AND DECISIONS

Read the complete original brief and inspect the environment. Create a concise implementation plan, requirement traceability table, proposed data model, access matrix, and explicit workflow transitions. Separate confirmed official requirements from team design choices and unresolved questions.

If I provide an official PS page, round invitation, or slide template, inspect it and record its exact version and constraints. If unavailable, keep the submission outline provisional and continue engineering against the supplied brief. Do not invent online-round judging weights, deadlines, slide limits, or mandatory AICTE disposal periods.

Compare three differentiators: institution timeline, evidence comparison workspace, and proposed-action overlap warnings. Select the timeline plus comparison workspace as the initial demonstration unless repository constraints justify a different choice. Treat action-overlap detection as an extension requiring structured action evidence.

Define proposed roles: RB officer, PGRC officer, regional officer, bureau supervisor/coordinator, senior management/competent authority, and system administrator. Distinguish coordination metadata from narratives, identities, and attachments. Administration privileges must not automatically imply unrestricted complaint access. Document this matrix as a prototype proposal requiring stakeholder approval.
Acceptance: every original requirement has an owner/stage; permissions and transitions are explicit; uncertain policies are listed; the next implementation slice is small enough to run end to end.
STAGE 1 — COPY-PASTE UI DESIGN PROMPT

Design and implement Samanvay as a calm, readable administrative workspace. A first-time judge should understand the problem and the next action within one screen. Every page must answer: What needs attention? Why? Who owns it? What can happen next?

Use a light background, dark readable typography, restrained blue navigation, amber attention indicators, and red only for urgent conditions or errors. Pair colors with meaningful text and icons. Avoid decorative charts, animated backgrounds, oversized hero sections, unexplained AI scores, and a chatbot that dominates the workflow. Use consistent spacing, labelled controls, visible keyboard focus, useful validation, and accessible status messages. Aim for WCAG 2.2 AA design practices; do not claim certified compliance.

Build the navigation around Overview, Cases, Institutions, Coordination, Reports, Notifications, and permitted Settings. Prioritize four demonstration screens: officer overview, institution profile, side-by-side evidence comparison, and case timeline. Also provide usable case intake/detail, report filters, notification history, and administrative settings. Desktop is primary; inspect narrower screens and zoomed layouts.

On the overview, show a short attention queue above workload charts. Each item states the issue, institution, owner, deadline, and primary action. Tables show case ID, institution, issue, bureau/officer, lifecycle, due date, and next action. Counts and charts must drill into the same filtered database records.

Use Demo Suryavan Institute, Pune, DEMO-INST-017, and the separate Demo Suryavan Institute, Nagpur, DEMO-INST-044. Identify every example as fictional. A fee-refund pair can be related while an independent faculty complaint remains separate at the Pune institution. Make the city/identifier distinction visible.

Place evidence, conflicting facts, and Confirm/Reject/Defer controls together. Label any temporary UI fixtures as illustrative. Replace them with real backend reads before claiming working functionality. Include loading, empty, error, permission-denied, stale-data, and retry states. No decorative clickable controls.

Acceptance: capture and inspect practical browser sizes; navigate the main path with keyboard; verify legibility, focus, labels, and overflow; document every control still awaiting backend integration.
STAGE 2 — BUILD THE PERSISTENT VERTICAL SLICE

Implement authentication, user scope, institution selection, complaint creation, assignment, and chronological history. Use migrations, seed commands, a secrets-free environment template, and documented startup commands.

Persist institutions and aliases; bureaus, regions, officers and roles; cases and sensitive complainant records; attachment metadata; assignment history; workflow events; and entity versions. Preserve original submitted institution text alongside its resolved identity. Case fields must include received date, subject, description, category, institution, lifecycle, owner, last action/date, next action, expected disposal date, and supporting evidence.

Use secure password hashing and appropriate session protection. Do not use a frontend role dropdown as authentication. If a demonstration persona switch exists, constrain it to an explicitly enabled development environment with synthetic accounts.

Implement an authenticated create-case API and detail API, validation errors, and an intake page that reports success only after the transaction succeeds. An uploaded file must become a real stored object, not just a filename in component state.

Acceptance: create a unique case through the UI, refresh, stop and restart the application, then retrieve the same case and history through the authenticated API and UI. Confirm the database row exists, unauthorized access fails, and overview counts change from actual records. Record the commands and observed evidence.
STAGE 3 — COMPLETE CASE WORKFLOWS AND ACCOUNTABILITY

Implement creation/import, assignment, review, information requests, transfer, escalation, disposal, and authorized reopening. Each transition requires permitted source states, appropriate authority, required reason/evidence, and an audit event. Disposal needs a resolution record; reopening retains the earlier disposal history. A rejected validation must leave state unchanged.

Keep pending/active definitions explicit. Under-process may be a subset of pending. Historical transfer counts must not be added to mutually exclusive lifecycle totals. Derive overdue from due date, lifecycle, and the configured clock. Define missing-date behavior.

Implement transfer initiation, acceptance, rejection, cancellation where permitted, and expiry handling. Source ownership remains until acceptance; target ownership and acceptance history update atomically. Only the authorized receiving role can accept. A coordinator role does not silently replace individual case ownership. Transfer must not automatically restart a disposal deadline.

Use optimistic version checks for edits and decisions. Return a clear conflict response when another user changed the record; provide reload/compare recovery. Use transactions and appropriate locking or constraints for acceptance and other coupled changes. Audit entries are append-only through application APIs; do not describe this as absolute tamper-proofing.

Acceptance: exercise valid/invalid transitions, rejected and accepted transfers, disposal/reopening, and simultaneous conflicting decisions. Verify one accountable owner, preserved case ID, unchanged state on failure, and complete history.
STAGE 4 — RESOLVE INSTITUTIONS AND ENABLE COORDINATION

Implement exact institution-ID lookup first, followed by normalized names, aliases, and address/location evidence. Require human confirmation for ambiguous identity. Similar names in Pune and Nagpur must not silently resolve to one institution. Keep provenance for confirmed aliases and identity decisions.

Create a deterministic coordination item whenever one confirmed institution has active cases in at least two distinct bureaus. The rule must work when the complaints are unrelated and when semantic services are unavailable. Display “Shared institution — coordination required”; reserve duplicate wording for individual relationship suggestions.

Persist coordination groups, participating cases, coordinating bureau/officer, notes, next actions, and review history. Keep original ownership and evidence. Show an institution timeline with concurrent bureau activity, deadlines, movements, and decisions.

Provide Confirm, Reject, and Defer decisions for suggested links. A rejected suggestion stays rejected for the same case versions and evidence fingerprint, including after refresh, scheduled processing, or restart. Materially changed evidence may create a new review item that references the earlier rejection; it must not erase that decision.

Acceptance: two unrelated active cross-bureau cases trigger institutional coordination without a duplicate label; one-bureau cases do not satisfy that rule; evidence decisions persist; similar-name institutions remain separate; all displayed information respects viewer permissions.
STAGE 5 — BUILD THE BASELINE AND OPTIONAL SEMANTIC MATCHER

Implement a transparent lexical/rule baseline using confirmed institution, normalized text, category, incident period, explicit references, relevant entities, and contradictory fields. Search a bounded eligible candidate set rather than repeatedly comparing every pair. Include relevant disposed cases in historical relationship search; active status is specific to the concurrent-bureau rule.

Define DUPLICATE, RELATED, INDEPENDENT, and UNKNOWN with examples. Different complainants or remedies concerning one event normally require separate related cases under our proposed annotation policy. Missing evidence should produce UNKNOWN or human review, not fabricated agreement.

Add cached local embeddings only after the baseline works. Record model/version, input construction, supported language assumptions, truncation/chunking behavior, and source versions. Optionally rerank retrieved candidates. Explain scores as ranking/evidence signals, not calibrated probabilities. Keep the enhanced method only if a measured comparison supports its value.

Validate any LLM response against a strict schema. Require source case IDs, exact excerpts or structured-field references, supporting and conflicting evidence, missing information, and proposed relationship. Verify citations against authorized supplied records. Treat complaints and documents as untrusted data; embedded instructions cannot invoke tools, alter permissions, or execute actions. Consequential controls remain in backend code.

When the model is unavailable, display “Semantic matching unavailable — rule-based checks active,” continue supported workflows, and do not fabricate semantic results. Recompute or mark stale suggestions after source changes.

Acceptance: demonstrate paraphrase retrieval, independent same-institution complaints, contradictory dates, ambiguous short descriptions, model outage, stale evidence, and prompt-injection text. Human approval remains necessary in every consequential path.
STAGE 6 — DEADLINES, NOTIFICATIONS, SEARCH, AND REPORTS

Implement persisted in-app notifications for coordination, potential relationships, pending actions, approaching deadlines, overdue conditions, escalation, and transfer events. Use deduplication keys, acknowledgement, and recorded delivery state. Retries and worker restarts must not create alert floods. External email may use a clearly labelled local test inbox.

Use configurable administrative rules, not invented official AICTE deadlines. Persist jobs or use a reliable database-backed equivalent. The same underlying scheduling logic must serve normal operation and tests. A demonstration clock belongs to an isolated synthetic demo context; advancing it must not alter host time or other users' deadlines. Guard clock/reset endpoints outside development/demo mode.
Implement search/filtering by institution name/ID, case ID, bureau, region, category, status, and date range. Apply scope before results, counts, snippets, and autocomplete are returned.

Provide bureau-, region-, institution-, and status-wise reports; ageing; disposal measures; relationship summaries; and monthly/quarterly views. Define calculations and denominators explicitly. Distinguish cohort disposal rates from disposals divided by new receipts, which can exceed 100% when clearing backlog. Specify date boundaries and time zone. Provide scoped CSV export and a readable printable report.

Acceptance: test just-before/at/after deadline boundaries, repeated scheduler runs, acknowledgement, worker restart, and isolated clock behavior. Confirm drill-down totals and exports agree with authorized underlying cases and documented formulas.
STAGE 7 — ENFORCE ACCESS AND ATTACHMENT SECURITY

Implement the proposed matrix in centralized backend policies combining role, bureau/region, case relationship, and explicit grants. Separate coordination metadata from full narrative, identity, and evidence. Management and system-administrator roles must follow their defined scopes rather than receiving accidental universal access.

Apply policies consistently to object reads/writes, list APIs, aggregate counts, matching candidate displays, source excerpts, notifications, search suggestions, reports, and exports. An internal matching service's broader processing permission does not authorize disclosure to every viewer. Return minimum authorized information and a clear route to request review by an appropriate coordinator.

Store attachments privately with generated storage keys. Validate allowed type, extension/signature, size, and authorization. Do not trust browser MIME declarations or expose storage directories publicly. Protect downloads separately from uploads. Keep secrets in environment configuration and sensitive narratives out of ordinary logs. Validate inputs and handle errors without exposing stack traces or credentials.

If adding database row-level security, verify with the actual application database role and document bypass behavior. Do not claim security from configuration alone. Record significant access and administrative actions without logging unnecessary personal data.

Acceptance: attempt direct API access using another case ID and attachment ID; test every role across search, matching evidence, notifications, counts, and exports. Test malformed uploads, forbidden transitions, session expiry, and unsafe model output. Record actual negative-test results and unresolved gaps.
STAGE 8 — BUILD THE DATASET AND RUN HONEST EVALUATION

Generate approximately 30–50 fictional institutions and 200–300 synthetic cases covering the original brief's edge cases. Include exact/paraphrased duplicates, related incidents, independent same-institution issues, name collisions, missing IDs, misspellings, incomplete text, conflicting dates, and all required workflow states. Keep explicit ground-truth labels outside model-visible case content.

Split development, validation, and held-out evaluation by incident families and near-duplicate generation templates. Do not randomly split pairs that share the same complaint or incident. Add an unseen-institution stress set. A held-out retrieval query needs a matching historical record in its held-out gallery; those incidents must remain unavailable for tuning. Ask humans to review difficult labels independently where possible and record disagreements.

Compare baseline and enhanced methods on the same held-out data. Measure institution matching, candidate recall at a stated k, per-class precision/recall/F1, class support, confusion matrix, UNKNOWN/abstention coverage, and end-to-end errors. Report latency with sample size, hardware, and cold/warm conditions. Do not turn synthetic accuracy into a claim about real AICTE complaints.

Run all fourteen acceptance scenarios in the original brief, including persistence after restart, real counts, cross-bureau alerts, semantic evidence, independent cases, institution collisions, decisions, transfers, reminders, escalation, unauthorized API/attachment access, export scope, AI outage, and concurrent updates. Inspect every meaningful UI control, keyboard flow, loading/error state, and practical screen size.

Acceptance: produce reproducible commands, raw results, labelled false positives/negatives, requirement-to-test evidence, limitations, and a clear distinction between measured outcomes and future targets. Fix material failures; report any remaining unfinished requirements explicitly.
STAGE 9 — JUDGE REHEARSAL AND RELEASE AUDIT

Prepare exact setup/startup instructions, migrations, seed commands, environment template, architecture/data-flow explanation, role matrix, matching explanation, baseline comparison, test evidence, limitations, and team module guide. Provide seeded synthetic credentials without production secrets. Implement an idempotent reset procedure gated to development/demo data; it must never delete an arbitrary configured production database.

Create an approximately three-minute rehearsal: PGRC receives a Pune fee-refund case; RB receives a paraphrase using an abbreviation; institution resolution and relationship evidence appear; an unrelated faculty case stays independent; an officer records coordination and next actions; the timeline shows accountability; an isolated demo clock triggers an alert; management exports the permitted institution report. Briefly demonstrate that the Nagpur institution is separate. Keep each claimed capability observable.

Prepare backup screenshots or a recording from the actual working build, labelled with its capture date/version. Verify all demo links, login credentials, reset commands, and model-cache availability. An official submission template overrides the provisional pitch outline when supplied; do not assume the panel will open external links or watch a long video.

Rehearse answers about differentiation, wrong matches, ownership, evidence, privacy, offline behavior, measured results, and simulated integrations. Ask a teammate unfamiliar with the build to explain the problem and next action from each key screen. Record confusion and repair the interface or narration.

Acceptance: run the complete demo from a clean reset, restart and repeat it, document observed results, and list unresolved limitations. Never promise selection or describe a planned feature, generated test, or mock integration as complete

paragraphs.text: SIH 26264 Research and Build Guide
Samanvay institution complaint coordination
Prepared 27 October 2026  |  Research and proposed implementation
Recommendation

Build Samanvay around one understandable officer decision: identify connected institutional activity, inspect the evidence, agree who coordinates the next action, and preserve every original complaint and its accountable owner. This gives the judges a clear reason for the system to exist and a concrete result to inspect.
The working value proposition is: Samanvay helps AICTE officers see connected complaints across bureaus, understand who owns each next step, and coordinate action while preserving every case.

The uploaded brief is a strong engineering specification. Its main risk is trying to demonstrate every feature with equal emphasis. Use the full brief as the implementation contract, but concentrate the presentation on the institution profile, evidence comparison, coordination decision and timeline.
The research finding that changes the pitch

CPGRAMS already describes an Intelligent Grievance Management System that detects repetitive grievances and analyses complaint meaning and topic clusters. A generic claim that AI detects duplicate complaints is therefore weak differentiation. The proposed advantage is the AICTE-specific connection between institution identity, bureau activity, evidence and accountable coordination. This is a product recommendation, not a claim that no comparable solution exists. [S2]
What this package establishes
A researched product direction, interface plan, technical architecture, evaluation protocol and submission narrative.
A separate copy-and-paste prompt pack for phased implementation by a coding assistant.
A conceptual interactive walkthrough using fictional records. It illustrates the proposed user experience; it is not a database-backed prototype or a measured AI system.
A clear boundary between demonstrated behaviour, implementation requirements and capabilities that need AICTE validation or authorised integration.

No application accuracy, time saving, security certification, official AICTE integration or selection outcome is claimed. Proposed rules and examples must remain labelled as illustrative until the relevant officials validate them.
Immediate input from the team

Obtain the official SIH26264 problem statement, current presentation template, round instructions and the deadline displayed for this specific problem. Check these with the institute SPOC today. The official portal could not be retrieved in full during this research, and indexed general deadlines conflict with a problem-specific date shown by independent mirrors. The roadmap below remains useful without assuming a deadline. [S1, S14]
Official requirements and judging evidence

The supplied brief identifies SIH26264 as Integrated Dashboard for Monitoring and Tracking Institution-Related Complaint Cases Across AICTE Bureaus/Cells, for AICTE Regulation Bureau, Software, Smart Automation. Independent current listings corroborate the ID and title. The full official problem page returned an access error, so the attachment remains the working requirement source pending portal confirmation. [U1, S14]

Indexed excerpts of the official SIH 2026 guideline identify novelty, complexity, clarity, detail in the prescribed format, feasibility, practicability, sustainability, scale of impact, user experience and future progression as evaluation considerations. The full current document and submission template were not retrievable. No official weights or mandatory three-minute demo rule were verified. [S1]
Consideration
Evidence this project should present
Problem relevance
One institution, simultaneous bureau activity, clear current owners and next actions.
Novelty
A completed cross-bureau coordination decision supported by explainable case relationships.
Clarity and user experience
A readable comparison screen and a task flow an unfamiliar viewer can explain.
Feasibility and practicability
Persistent records, working transfers, permissions, reminders and scoped exports.
Impact and future progression
Measured prototype behaviour plus an honest path to an authorised operational pilot.
Design for both possible online formats

For asynchronous idea screening, the submitted slides or PDF must explain the problem, novelty and proof without a presenter. Include one annotated workflow image, a concise architecture and a visible results table. A video or preview link is supplementary unless the current instructions say otherwise; do not depend on judges opening it.

For a live online presentation, rehearse a three-minute walkthrough as a useful unit, then adapt it to the actual time limit. Begin already signed into a synthetic demo account. Show one complete decision rather than narrating every menu.
What remains to be confirmed
Exact current problem text and any clarifications from AICTE.
Current template, slide or file limits, accepted link formats and round timing.
The problem-specific submission deadline and the SPOC nomination requirements.
Any originality, AI-tool disclosure or external-service instructions. Do not assume blanket permission or prohibition for AI-generated code.
Official bureau allocation rules, access boundaries and disposal policies before any real deployment.

A separate DARPG challenge in 2024 explicitly asked for improvements to officer usability of IGMS and the Tree Dashboard. That is useful domain evidence for prioritising administrative usability; its contest rules and datasets do not apply to this SIH submission. [S3]
Product choices and changes to the brief
Approach
Value and risk
Decision
Institution coordination workspace
Exposes parallel bureau work and responsibility. It must offer a next action to avoid becoming a passive reporting page.
Primary product
Explainable relationship review
Finds likely connections despite wording differences. Its value depends on visible evidence and careful handling of uncertainty.
Build alongside coordination
Overlap between proposed actions
Could reveal two draft requests for the same records. Harder to validate and may imply procedural equivalence.
Add after the core works

The selected combination is a coordination workspace, evidence comparison and shared institution timeline. Together these explain discovery, review, responsibility and follow-through. A relationship graph or general chatbot should be added only if user testing shows a specific benefit.
Refine the implementation contract
Issue to resolve
Required clarification
One enormous execution prompt
Keep the uploaded brief as the contract and run smaller phases with observable acceptance conditions.
Ambiguous status counts
Separate lifecycle, ownership, transfer state, overdue condition and escalation. Define every report denominator.
Duplicate versus related
Define labels before generating data. Different complainants with independent remedies usually need related case handling.
AI score presentation
Show evidence and uncertainty. Similarity scores are not calibrated probabilities.
Synthetic evaluation leakage
Keep incident groups and near-identical template families out of multiple evaluation splits.
Coordination visibility
Publish only authorised metadata; evidence excerpts, counts and notifications also need access checks.
Deadline and reset behaviour
Keep demo time isolated from production rules and make reset destructive only inside a disposable demo environment.
What should be built deeply first

The first complete slice is login, complaint creation, institution resolution, persisted owner and case timeline. Next add a second bureau case, generate the institution coordination item, inspect supporting evidence, and save a human decision. This sequence proves the central value early while leaving a stable foundation for the remaining requirements.

Keep every feature in the original brief on the requirement map. Lower presentation priority does not remove a requirement. Mark each item as implemented and verified, implemented but not verified, planned or blocked. A screenshot alone proves only the appearance shown in that screenshot.
Relationships and the demonstration dataset

Institution identity, complaint relationship and coordination responsibility are different concepts. Store and display them separately. The following operational definitions are proposed for the prototype and require stakeholder confirmation for real use.
Relationship
Evidence required
Result
Same institution across bureaus
Confirmed institution identity and active cases in at least two current bureaus.
Create a coordination item regardless of complaint similarity.
Possible duplicate submission
Evidence of the same incident and substantially the same complainant or request, subject to uncertainty.
Suggest a human review; retain both original records.
Related complaints
Shared event or issue but distinct complainants, evidence or remedies.
Link for context and coordination; retain independent case handling.
Independent cases at one institution
Common institution but different issues or events.
Keep cases separate while displaying institutional context.
Insufficient information
Identity, incident or complainant evidence is missing or contradictory.
Ask for review or clarification; abstain from a confident label.
Use one clear fictional story
All institutions, people, receipts and allegations below are invented. Bureau allocations and deadlines are demonstration assumptions, not statements about AICTE rules.
Record
Demonstration fact
Expected handling
PGRC 014
Demo Suryavan Institute, Pune; student token DEMO-STU-042; receipt R-882 for a 42,000-rupee refund.
Original refund complaint.
RB 023
DSI Pune; same synthetic student token and receipt, differently worded description.
Resolve institution alias; suggest possible duplicate with evidence.
PGRC 019
Same Pune institution; faculty salary grievance for a different period.
Same institution coordination remains relevant; complaint stays separate.
Other institution
Demo Suryavan Institute, Nagpur; DEMO-INST-044 instead of Pune DEMO-INST-017.
Keep institution identity separate despite the similar name.

An additional evaluation case should change the complainant while retaining the same refund event. Its expected relationship becomes related rather than automatically duplicate. Another should remove the incident date and reference; the appropriate result may be insufficient information.

Do not silently resolve an institution from its abbreviation alone. Show the ID, city, alias source and any conflicting attributes. A newly confirmed alias needs provenance and an authorised review rather than automatic promotion from a model guess.
Interface structure for officers and judges

Each screen should make the attention item, reason, owner and available action visible. The officer landing page should be a short action queue. Management can have a separate default view of workload and trends.
Screen
What it makes clear
Primary action
My work
Coordination needed, pending transfer acceptance, approaching deadlines and overdue work.
Review the relevant item
Cases
Searchable records with institution, owner, lifecycle, due date and next action.
Open or create a case
Institution profile
Confirmed identity, aliases, active bureau involvement and consolidated history.
Open coordination
Case detail
Current accountable officer, facts, evidence, next action and movement history.
Record action or request transfer
Coordination
Side-by-side evidence, contradictions, relationship decision and coordinating lead.
Confirm, keep separate or defer
Reports
Filtered totals, definitions, underlying cases and authorised outputs.
Drill down or export
Notifications
Grouped changes requiring attention, acknowledgement and destination links.
Review or acknowledge
Visual decisions

Use a restrained administrative interface with dark readable text, neutral surfaces and one main accent colour. Reserve colour for meaningful statuses and always pair it with a text label. Show the current role, scope filters, data freshness and synthetic-data label. Expand Regulation Bureau and Public Grievance Redressal Cell at first use.

Use approximately 16-pixel body text and generous table row spacing as initial design choices, then verify at the actual screen-sharing size. Keep long details in a case page rather than shrinking the whole table. Primary buttons should name the action: Review evidence, Confirm related cases, Keep separate, Request transfer or Accept transfer.

GIGW 3.0 explicitly emphasises user-centred information architecture and includes WCAG 2.1 Level AA. W3C specifies minimum normal-text contrast of 4.5:1, with defined exceptions and a lower threshold for large text. Keyboard operation, visible focus and explicit form labels belong in the acceptance checks. [S4, S5, S6]

WCAG 2.2 adds a 24 by 24 CSS-pixel minimum target-size criterion with exceptions. Aim for larger important controls as a usability choice; do not misattribute this addition to GIGW's published WCAG 2.1 baseline. Claim conformance only after a full assessment. [S7]
States that must be designed

Include loading, empty, failed, retry, validation, unauthorised and stale-update states. A success message appears after a persisted backend operation. A count or chart must open the records behind it. Provide a useful narrow-screen layout even though the primary demonstration is desktop-first.
The signature coordination workspace

The centre of the demonstration should be a side-by-side review that ends with a recorded decision. A judge should see the evidence and the change in responsibility without needing an explanation of embeddings.
Top of the screen

State why the item exists: Two bureaus have active cases at Demo Suryavan Institute, Pune. Display the institution ID and both current case owners. This institution-level signal remains true even if the officer rejects a duplicate suggestion.
Evidence comparison

Show the two case IDs, subjects and short source excerpts. Separate supporting facts, contradictory facts and missing facts. For the refund example, a common synthetic receipt and complainant token support the suggestion; different dates or amounts must remain visible. Do not hide contradictions inside a confidence number.
Use source references that can be opened by authorised viewers. A restricted viewer sees only approved coordination metadata; a matching excerpt must not become a way to bypass access controls.
Decision and next action

Offer Confirm duplicate relationship, Confirm related cases, Keep separate and Defer for clarification. Require a concise reason. Separately capture the coordinating bureau, coordinating officer, next action and due date. Make clear that choosing a coordination lead does not transfer the original cases.

A useful action might be: PGRC coordinates a single request for the refund records; RB reviews its own case after the response. This is illustrative workflow content. Each bureau retains the authority to act within its validated responsibilities.
After the decision

Display the recorded relationship, decision maker, reason and time. Add the coordination action to the institution timeline. Preserve the original complaint text, attachments and ownership. Rejected suggestions should stay rejected for the same evidence versions; a materially changed record can reopen review with an explanation.
Condition
Recommended wording
Shared institution
Two bureaus have active cases. Review coordination.
Possible duplicate
Both records refer to the same refund request. Officer review required.
Uncertainty
Incident date is missing. More information is needed.
Independent issue
Same institution, separate faculty grievance.
Transfer pending
The current officer remains responsible until acceptance.
AI unavailable
Semantic matching is unavailable. Institution checks and rule-based matching continue.

The interactive concept accompanying this report demonstrates this navigation and local decision state only. The production prototype must replace local interactions with authenticated API calls, persistent records and tested permissions.
Architecture and data model

Use a modular application that the team can run and explain. A practical default is React with TypeScript, a FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL with migrations, private attachment storage and one worker for matching and deadlines. Adapt to an existing team stack if it already supports the same guarantees.
Component
Responsibility
Frontend
Officer screens, accessible tables, evidence comparison and task-specific forms.
Backend
Authentication, case-level authorisation, validated workflow commands and report queries.
Database
Canonical institutions, cases, owners, relationships, transfers, notifications and audit events.
Worker
Retryable matching and reminder jobs, deduplicated notifications and deadline policy checks.
Private file storage
Evidence bytes accessed through authorised download endpoints.
Optional model adapters
Local semantic candidates or constrained case briefs; deterministic fallback remains available.
Data flow

An officer submits a case through the frontend. The API validates the request and permissions, then commits the case and audit event. A persistent job or outbox entry triggers institution coordination checks and relationship retrieval. Results are stored, filtered for the viewing role and displayed for human review. An authorised decision is committed with a reason, versions and timeline event. Audit events are append-only through application APIs; corrections add a new event. This does not establish protection against a privileged database administrator.
Core records
Institution and institution alias: canonical ID, supplied name, confirmed identity, location and confirmation provenance.
Case and current assignment: stable case ID, received date, original narrative, category, lifecycle, owner, next action, due date and record version.
Transfer: source, destination, initiator, reason, request time, acceptance or rejection and outcome.
Relationship suggestion and decision: case pair, proposed label, evidence, conflicts, model or rule version, input versions and officer decision.
Coordination group and task: institution, participating cases, lead, action, responsible officer and due date.
Attachment, access grant, audit event, notification and deadline policy: separate records with appropriate retention and disclosure controls.
Implementation boundaries

For a few hundred complaints, exact comparison over a scoped candidate set is a reasonable starting design. A separate vector database service and approximate index are not necessary to establish the concept. pgvector supports exact search and optional approximate indexes; approximate search trades retrieval recall for speed. Add it only when measurements justify it. [S9]

Pin compatible dependencies, provide a repeatable startup command and document the actual tested environment. An integration adapter should preserve external source IDs and provenance, support idempotent imports, and clearly label synthetic sources. Do not imply access to an AICTE API until one is actually authorised and connected.
Workflow ownership and report definitions
Keep operational dimensions separate

A proposed lifecycle is Received, Assigned, Under review, Awaiting information and Disposed. Reopening is an authorised action with a reason that restores an active state. Transfer request status, escalation level and overdue condition are separate attributes. This avoids contradictory counts and allows a case to be under review, overdue and awaiting transfer acceptance at the same time.
Make transfer an explicit handoff

The source officer requests transfer and records the reason. The destination accepts or rejects. Until acceptance, the source remains the accountable owner. Acceptance commits the ownership change, transfer outcome and history event together. Rejection or expiry leaves a visible responsible owner. Do not reset the original deadline silently; any adjustment needs an authorised reason and policy reference.

Use a version field on cases and coordination decisions. If two officers edit the same version, the second conflicting update should return a clear conflict and preserve the earlier decision. SQLAlchemy documents version counters for detecting stale rows; the chosen implementation must also account for operations that bypass ORM version checks. [S10]
Define dashboard calculations before coding
Measure
Proposed definition
Total cases
Distinct permitted case IDs in the stated population and date scope.
Pending
Cases not currently disposed. Under review is a subset, not an additional disjoint category.
Overdue
An active case whose applicable due time is earlier than the report as-of time.
Case age
Elapsed calendar days from received time to the as-of time for active cases; explain any working-day alternative.
Transfers completed
Transfer acceptance events in a stated period, labelled separately from cases awaiting acceptance.
Disposal rate
For a defined received-date cohort: cases currently disposed as of the cutoff divided by all cases in that cohort.
Monthly disposals
Distinct cases with a disposal event in the month. Reopened cases and repeat disposal events are reported separately.

Reports must state whether bureau means current owner or owner at the event time. Preserve assignment history to answer both. Use the same case-permission rules in dashboard queries, search and exports. Include the report period, cutoff time and definitions in printable output.
Reminders and escalation

Store policy versions and compute alerts from persisted due dates. Use a uniqueness key for case, rule, threshold and due-date version so repeated worker runs do not spam the officer. Persist acknowledgements. Demonstration escalation may notify a supervisor; it must not silently change case ownership or invent a mandated AICTE timetable.
Matching and constrained use of AI
Two engines with separate purposes

The coordination engine groups active cases by confirmed institution and counts distinct current bureaus. It creates or updates an institution-level coordination item when multiple bureaus are involved. It does not need language similarity and does not establish that the proposed actions conflict.

The relationship engine retrieves candidate cases and assesses the incident evidence. It should include relevant historical disposed cases, because a new submission may refer to a previously handled event. Active status restricts the concurrent-work alert, not every historical relationship search.
Recommended matching sequence
Resolve institution identity from a valid exact ID, or use normalised names, confirmed aliases and location. Preserve the original supplied text and abstain when ambiguous.
Retrieve candidates from the authorised processing scope. Use institution, category and incident context without making every missing field a hard exclusion.
Implement an explainable baseline with tokens or character features, incident references, dates, amounts and contradiction rules.
Add cached sentence embeddings to help retrieve paraphrases. Optionally rerank a limited candidate set; test whether it improves the actual evaluation set.
Store supporting excerpts, conflicts, missing fields, method version and input versions. Require human confirmation before a relationship affects coordination.

Sentence Transformers documents a retrieve-then-rerank pattern. Its suitability for this project must be established by baseline comparison, not assumed from the documentation. Similarity measures rank candidates; they do not by themselves prove duplication. [S8]

An English starting option is all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Its published model card describes a short-text encoder with default truncation beyond 256 word pieces. Long complaints need deliberate segmentation and evidence extraction so key contradictions are not lost. Record the model version, licence, download requirement and language coverage. [S11]
Use generative AI only where it helps

Useful optional tasks include extracting incident fields and drafting a case brief from authorised evidence. Require validated structured output with proposed relationship, source case IDs, field names, exact excerpts, conflicts, missing information and a human-review flag. Reject invented source references and excerpts absent from the supplied case version.

Complaint text and attachments are untrusted data. The model must not have permission to transfer, close, merge, message or change access controls. Validate model outputs and enforce permissions outside the model; prompt wording alone is not a security boundary. If a model fails, display the unavailable state and continue with the core workflow and baseline checks. [S12]

The following matrix is a proposed prototype policy. It is not an official AICTE access allocation. Roles should be combined with bureau, region, case assignment and explicit coordination grants. A coordinator is not automatically entitled to every complainant detail.

Own-case actions; request transfer; permitted relationship review.

Assigned or authorised PGRC cases; approved coordination metadata.
Own-case actions; request transfer; permitted relationship review.

Enforcement requirements

Deny access unless a policy permits it. Check every backend request, including direct case URLs, attachment downloads, matching evidence, autocomplete, counts, notifications and exports. OWASP specifically recommends default denial and permission validation on every request. Hiding a button is only a user-interface behaviour. [S13]

Separate approved coordination metadata from personal narratives and attachments. A bureau may need the other case ID, officer and pending administrative action without receiving an unredacted complaint. The internal matching service may have an explicitly broader processing scope, but its results must pass the viewing officer's disclosure policy.

Store evidence privately, use generated storage names and enforce file type, signature and size controls. A browser-supplied content type is not sufficient validation. Serve evidence through authorised handlers, keep sensitive values out of logs and use environment-based secrets. These are consistent with OWASP upload guidance. [S15]
Security proof for the demonstration
A user without case access cannot fetch the case by guessing its API identifier.
The same restriction applies to attachments, exported rows and matching excerpts.
A malformed or stale decision is rejected and does not change the case.
A document containing instructions to close a case is treated as evidence text, not an application command.
Passwords are handled by an established authentication implementation; demo credentials are clearly isolated from any real deployment.

For real deployment, validate the data-sharing agreement, retention schedule, hosting arrangement, audit requirements, accessibility review, incident response and authorised bureau policies. The prototype cannot demonstrate compliance merely by displaying a security badge.
Synthetic data and credible evaluation

Start with the supplied target of 30 to 50 fictional institutions and 200 to 300 synthetic complaints. Keep a small, repeatable demonstration scenario separately from the evaluation corpus. No real student identity or allegation against a real institution is needed. [U1]
Label before tuning

Define canonical institution identities, incident groups, complainant tokens and relationship labels first. Include exact and paraphrased duplicates, related but distinct complainants, independent complaints at one institution, similar names in different cities, missing IDs, spelling errors, conflicting dates and insufficient descriptions. Have a second team member review the difficult labels and record disagreements.

Split incident groups and template families before model tuning. Do not randomly split complaint pairs so that the same incident appears on both sides. Add a separate unseen-institution stress set. Grouped evaluation is a standard way to avoid overlapping correlated groups; this incident-based application is the proposed evaluation design. [S16]

In a retrieval test, the held-out query still needs its correct historical counterpart in the test gallery. Keeping incident groups out of training and threshold tuning does not mean deleting the record the system should retrieve.
What to measure
Report with the result
Institution resolution
Accuracy, abstention or review rate, missing-ID results and similar-name errors.
Candidate retrieval
Recall at a stated candidate limit, including cases missed before classification.
Case relationship
Per-class precision, recall and F1; class counts and a confusion matrix.
End-to-end behaviour
Include institution-resolution failures and retrieval misses; show uncertainty coverage.
Core coordination rule
Tests for same institution across bureaus, one bureau, disposed cases and ambiguous identity.
Latency
Number of runs, hardware, dataset size, cold or warm model, median and 95th percentile.
Usability
Task completion, time, errors and observed confusion for a stated participant sample.
Compare the same cases

Evaluate the lexical baseline and enhanced matcher on the same frozen held-out cases. Tune thresholds only on development or validation data. If the enhancement does not improve useful performance, retain the simpler method and explain the result. A prototype can be credible without a large model.

Do not present one unexplained AI accuracy figure. Show false positives, false negatives and cases sent for review. Synthetic performance does not establish real-world or national-scale accuracy. State targets, observed measurements and future goals separately.
Acceptance tests that prove the core

The following tests correspond to the supplied brief. Record the exact command, environment, expected behaviour, observed outcome and evidence. Test code written is not the same as test code executed. [U1]
Test
Expected observable result
Persistence
Create a case, refresh and restart the service; the same case and history remain.
Database totals
Create, dispose or reopen a case; relevant dashboard values change from stored records.
Shared institution
Two active bureaus at one confirmed institution generate a coordination item.
Paraphrased duplicate
The differently worded refund case is suggested with inspectable evidence.
Independent complaint
The faculty grievance remains separate while sharing institutional context.
Name collision
Similar institution names in different cities are not silently combined.
Officer decision
Confirmation, rejection and deferral persist; repeated jobs do not overwrite them.
Transfer
Source remains responsible until acceptance; history survives the atomic handoff.
Reminder
Crossing the configured approaching-deadline threshold produces one notification.
Escalation
Overdue behaviour follows the selected policy and remains correct after worker restart.
Direct access
An unauthorised API case read and attachment request are rejected.
Export scope
CSV and printable output contain only permitted fields and records.
AI failure
Disabled or failed semantic service leaves workflow and deterministic checks usable.
Concurrent edit
A stale update produces a clear conflict and does not silently overwrite a decision.
Additional tests worth the time

Repeat the notification job to prove deduplication, edit evidence to invalidate an old suggestion, and check that a confirmed relationship does not grant extra access. Confirm that transfer does not reset age or deadline without an authorised reason. Verify that the demo clock and reset routes are unavailable outside the demo environment.
Browser inspection

Run the important tasks in the browser at the intended screen-share size and a narrow viewport. Check readable evidence, keyboard navigation, focus, error recovery, permission states and every visible control. Inspect a printable report. Record any failed requirement in the limitation list rather than marking the whole prototype complete.
How to build with AI prompting

Use AI in two distinct ways. A coding assistant can help implement and test the application. The application itself may use local semantic matching or a constrained language model. Success with the first does not prove correctness of the second. The team remains responsible for domain decisions, evaluation labels, permissions and the final explanation.

Keep the uploaded specification and this guide as context. The companion prompt pack provides a master contract and phased instructions. Run each phase to its acceptance conditions; keep the same schema, API contract and project state file across sessions.
Phase
Completion condition
Requirements and contracts
Definitions, schema, access matrix, state transitions and requirement map are written.
Persistent working slice
Login, create case, owner, timeline and restart persistence work.
Core operations
Review, information request, disposal, reopening and transfer work with reasons.
Institution coordination
Aliases and name collisions are handled; multi-bureau activity produces an item.
Relationship review
Baseline evidence, confirm/reject/defer and separate coordination ownership persist.
Reminders and reports
Persisted alerts, deadline simulation, drilldowns and scoped exports work.
Optional semantic matching
Cached model, graceful fallback and honest baseline comparison are implemented.
Verification
Acceptance tests, concurrency, permissions and browser tasks run and failures are fixed.
Presentation
Reset, rehearsal script, screenshots, real results and limitations are ready.
Use explicit evidence at every handoff

Require the coding assistant to report changed files, commands actually run, observed results, unresolved failures and the next phase. A completion message without evidence is insufficient. Preserve a progress file so a new session continues the existing work rather than rebuilding a second incompatible version.
Assign human ownership

With six team members, allocate product and presentation, frontend and accessibility, backend and workflow, matching and evaluation, security and integration testing, and synthetic data plus demo operations. This is a suggested work split, not a verified rule on team size. With fewer members, combine adjacent responsibilities.

Reserve time for reviewing confusing screens and rehearsing. A sensible planning allocation is roughly one half implementation, one quarter testing and repair, and one quarter explanation and submission preparation. Treat this as a starting allocation, not a delivery promise; available time and team capability may change it.
Three minute demonstration and backup

This is a recommended rehearsal script, not a verified SIH time limit. Prepare the first complaint and prefill the second so the audience watches a meaningful decision rather than data entry. Every record and deadline rule must be visibly synthetic or illustrative.
Time
Screen action and narration
Open the attention queue. Explain that different bureaus can handle the same institution without seeing each other's work.
Submit the prepared RB refund complaint using an institution abbreviation. Show the confirmed identity and existing PGRC activity.
Open the comparison. Point to the refund reference, incident facts and uncertainty; distinguish the institution signal from the complaint suggestion.
Record the relationship decision, coordination lead and next action. Show that both original owners remain accountable.
Show the separate faculty complaint and similar-name Nagpur institution. Explain why neither is automatically combined.
Show the timeline and a prepared transfer handoff. Advance the labelled demo clock to display a configured reminder or escalation.
Open the consolidated institution report, drill into the records and export. End on the owner and next action.
Opening and closing lines

Opening: Two bureaus may receive complaints about the same institution, yet work without a shared view. Samanvay brings the cases, evidence and responsibilities together so officers can decide how to coordinate.
Closing: Every complaint remains intact. Officers see why a connection is suggested, record who coordinates the next step, and retain a traceable history of the decision.
Prepare for a failed connection

Keep a real 60-second recording of the same implemented sequence: second case, evidence, human decision and updated timeline. Keep readable screenshots as a final fallback and label them accurately. The recording must show the application that actually exists, not an animation presented as functioning software.
Rehearsal checks
Start the application, sign in and reset the demo before the presentation.
Preload optional local models and verify the core with AI disabled.
Use one presenter and one operator with agreed handoffs.
Rehearse at the actual screen-share resolution; enlarge evidence if needed.
Have another team member run the entire sequence from the written instructions.
Keep architecture, test evidence and known limitations ready for questions.
Submission narrative and judge questions
Provisional six part pitch
Map this content into the current official template when supplied. Six parts are recommended for clarity; they are not a verified slide-count requirement.
Part
Message and supporting evidence
Problem
Parallel bureau activity at one institution creates uncertainty over ownership and coordinated action. Show one concrete example.
Solution
Samanvay connects institutional activity and turns it into an accountable review. Show the main workspace.
Distinctive behaviour
Separate shared institution, possible duplicate, related and independent complaints. Show evidence and the counterexample.
How it works
Present identity resolution, a reliable workflow, optional semantic retrieval and human decisions in a compact architecture.
Feasibility and validation
Show actual persistence, transfer, permission and evaluation results with dataset size and limitations.
Impact and deployment
Explain the potential operational benefit and the authorised data, integration and policy work needed for a pilot.
Answers the team should be able to defend
Judge question
Concise answer
How is this different?
It connects institution identity to cross-bureau work and records a coordination decision with visible ownership.
Why use AI?
Language matching may find paraphrased incidents. Exact identity and active-bureau checks remain deterministic.
What if matching is wrong?
Officers inspect evidence, reject or defer suggestions, and keep all original complaints.
Who owns a transferred case?
The source retains responsibility until acceptance under the proposed handoff policy.
What is actually integrated?
Name only tested integrations; identify synthetic imports and proposed adapters explicitly.
How accurate or useful is it?
Give the actual held-out results and observed usability findings, with sample size and limitations.

Do not claim universal accuracy, guaranteed selection, certified security, absolute tamper-proof history or a quantified productivity improvement without the corresponding evidence. A readable limitation is more defensible than a demonstration that fails under one follow-up question.

Check comprehension before polishing more screens

Ask three to five people who have not seen the project to watch a short explanation. Then ask: What problem is solved? Why are these cases connected? Who owns the next step? What happens to the unrelated complaint? Who makes the linking decision? Record the answers and the points of confusion. This is a formative rehearsal, not a representative user study.

A useful internal acceptance goal is that each viewer can explain the common institution, independent complaints, current owner and officer decision. If they cannot, simplify the screen or story before adding another feature.
Questions for an authorised AICTE stakeholder
Which systems receive cases, and what stable external identifiers can be imported?
How are institution IDs and aliases validated, and how are unresolved identities handled?
Which metadata may be shared across bureaus and who can read the original evidence?
Who initiates and accepts transfers, and what happens if acceptance is delayed?
Which deadlines apply to each case type, and when may they be extended or paused?
Who can reopen a disposed case, confirm relationships and appoint a coordination lead?
Which reports and retention rules are operationally required?
A real deployment would need more evidence

Validate the proposed rules with officers, map authorised integrations, review privacy and retention obligations, test on approved representative data, and conduct operational, security and accessibility reviews. Establish hosting, backups, monitoring, incident response and named maintenance ownership. A synthetic hackathon prototype can demonstrate the workflow, but it cannot establish readiness for unrestricted government use.

The immediate decision is to build the persistent coordination workflow and its evidence screen first. The companion prompts provide the implementation sequence; the official template and deadline should determine how that evidence is packaged for the online round.
